claims.statement: In a meta-analysis of five placebo-controlled trials of bupropion or modafinil in people with methamphetamine dependence (642 participants), urine-verified abstinence in the final two weeks of treatment was about one in five with medication and with placebo (70 of 353, 19.8%, vs 62 of 289, 21.5%; OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.65–1.45; 5 fewer per 1,000, from 64 fewer to 69 more), with no difference between the two drugs. No dexamphetamine or methylphenidate trial entered this analysis. Across 14 trials of the four drugs, retention to the end of treatment was 53.0% vs 48.0% (OR 1.20, 0.91–1.58).
claims.magnitude: Abstinence 19.8% vs 21.5%, OR 0.97 (0.65–1.45), I² 2%; 5 fewer per 1,000 (64 fewer to 69 more). Retention 53.0% vs 48.0%, OR 1.20 (0.91–1.58), I² 15%.
